headline: Agilent, a laboratory technology company, has agreed to buy Proscia, a maker of digital pathology and AI software, for $240 million in cash plus up to $30 million more if performance goals are met.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a signed, officially announced acquisition in AI-assisted pathology, though the price is modest and the deal has not closed.
importance_line: Laboratories and hospitals that read tissue slides on screen may soon get AI analysis tools bundled with Agilent's testing products, but the deal is not yet closed and the usage and revenue figures come from the companies.
summary: HIT Consultant reports, citing Agilent's announcement of 13 Oct 2026, that Agilent has signed a definitive agreement to buy Proscia, whose Concentriq software helps laboratories and hospitals manage digital pathology (tissue samples examined as scanned images on a computer) and AI analysis tools, for $240 million in cash at closing plus up to $30 million tied to future milestones. Agilent chief executive Padraig McDonnell said the purchase expands the company's presence in a fast-growing field, and HIT Consultant adds that Proscia's software is used in over 4,000 laboratories, health systems and clinics and that the two firms have sold together since a September 2022 distribution agreement.
